legend: A permutation of size N%%ZSMJ0%% is a sequence of N%%ZSMJ1%% positive integers containing the numbers 1%%ZSMJ2%% to N%%ZSMJ3%% where each number appears exactly once in the sequence. For example, [1,4,5,3,2]%%ZSMJ4%% is a permutation of size 5%%ZSMJ5%%, while [1,1,4,3,5]%%ZSMJ6%% and [1,6,2,3,4]%%ZSMJ7%% are not.

We can compare two permutations using lexicographical order. For two permutations p%%ZSMJ8%% and p%%ZSMJ9%% of the same size N%%ZSMJ10%% where p=[a1,a2,...,aN]%%ZSMJ11%% and q=[b1,b2,...,bN]%%ZSMJ12%%, we define p%%ZSMJ13%% is smaller than q%%ZSMJ14%% if and only if there exists an index i%%ZSMJ15%% such that aj=bj%%ZSMJ16%% for every j<i%%ZSMJ17%% and ai<bi%%ZSMJ18%%. For example, [1,3,4,2,5]%%ZSMJ19%% is ordered before [1,3,5,2,4]%%ZSMJ20%%.

Two permutations p%%ZSMJ21%% and q%%ZSMJ22%% of size N%%ZSMJ23%% are considered an ideal pair if, when all N!%%ZSMJ24%% permutations of size N%%ZSMJ25%% are arranged in a circle based on lexicographic order, permutation p%%ZSMJ26%% and permutation q%%ZSMJ27%% are positioned directly opposite each other in the circle.
Given a permutation p%%ZSMJ29%%, your task is to identify the permutation q%%ZSMJ30%% that together forms an ideal pair.
input: The first line contains one integer N%%ZSMJ31%% (2≤N≤1,000,000)%%ZSMJ32%% — size of the permutation.
The second line contains N%%ZSMJ33%% distinct integers from 1%%ZSMJ34%% to N%%ZSMJ35%% — the given permutation p%%ZSMJ36%%.
output: One line contains N%%ZSMJ37%% distinct integers that are the permutation that forms an ideal pair with permutation p%%ZSMJ38%%.
